$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.imports. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-IMPORT-THRESHOLD-ONE
arms.note: one surviving occurrence is enough to buy an import line, so the wash the threshold exists to refuse is written anyway

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-DECLARER-READS
arms.note: the module an ambient statement IMPORTS counts as one of the statement's readers, so its own declaration of that type keeps the statement alive and a stale one in a root ambient source is never reportable

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-DECLARER-READS-USING
arms.note: the declaring module is dropped from the reader set for a `using` as well as for an import, so an ambient `using` that a module calling its own statics extension-style depends on reads as dead and is deleted

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-REDUNDANT-GUARDED-SKIP
arms.note: the search for the group that decides a name skips one whose only binder is `#if`-guarded and lands on a farther identical group, so deleting the module's own statement retargets the name in the builds that guard is on

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-REDUNDANT-USING-POSITION
arms.note: a `using` is treated as binding only a name, so an own statement an ambient source repeats is deleted although another `using` in scope then takes the position it held and every method both modules declare resolves elsewhere

arms.name: M-HOIST-NEVER-SOUND
arms.note: no statement is ever judged safe to add to an ambient source, so the rule proposes nothing at all and the whole hoist is inert

arms.name: M-HOIST-RETARGET-BAND
arms.note: a second declaration of the imported simple name is never a retarget, so the ambient statement silently replaces a same-package, root-package or wildcard-reached namesake in the modules that never spelled it

arms.name: M-HOIST-USING-DEMOTION
arms.note: a `using` is lifted out of a module that keeps another one, so the extension it held loses its position to the rival that stays and every method both modules declare resolves elsewhere

arms.name: M-HOIST-CHAIN-INHERITED
arms.note: a statement the chain above a directory already puts in force is proposed again, so a nested ambient source repeats its own parent

arms.name: M-HOIST-GUARDED-BLIND
arms.find: if (imp.guarded || SymbolIndex.bindsAnyOf(imp, statement.names, ctx.publicTypes)) return false;
arms.note: a chain carrying a `#if`-guarded statement is added to anyway, so a position this rule writes joins a chain whose every resolution answers the union of two build configurations

arms.name: M-HOIST-SHORT-CHAIN
arms.note: a governed module whose chain is knowingly SHORT is judged anyway, so the statement is added against bindings the engine never saw

arms.name: M-HOIST-MIN-MODULES
arms.note: a directory with too few modules for a share to mean anything is weighed anyway, so one module of two carries the whole verdict

arms.name: M-HOIST-SITE-ORDER
arms.note: the narrowest position is weighed first, so a statement lands in a nested source AND in its parent and the nested copy repeats what the parent already puts in force

arms.name: M-RUN-GATE-NO-INDEX
arms.note: the report reads no index, so it never admits a wildcard the fix would sort

arms.name: M-FIX-GATE-NO-INDEX
arms.note: the fix reads no index, so it splits a reported block at the wildcard and sorts each piece instead of the block

arms.name: M-WEDGE-WILDCARD-LIFTED
arms.note: a wildcard member below a wedged `using` is lifted into the merged block above the group

arms.name: M-WEDGE-WILDCARD-CROSSES-USING
arms.note: a wildcard between two wedged `using` groups is left below the merged group, crossing the later one

arms.name: M-UNUSED-VALUES-BLIND
arms.note: a module import kept alive only by a bare module-level field or constructor is deleted — the only binder breaks the build, the LAST of two silently rebinds

arms.name: M-UNUSED-VALUES-UNLISTED-DELETED
arms.find: if (!membersByPath.exists(imp.raw) || (typeValues != null && fieldValues != null)) return false;
arms.note: a known module whose constructors cannot be listed is deleted on its type names alone

arms.name: M-REDUNDANT-VALUES-BLIND
arms.note: a sub-type import is deleted though a third line binds one of its constructors, so the bare name moves to that line

arms.name: M-REDUNDANT-AMBIENT-VALUES
arms.note: an own enum import duplicated by the ambient source is deleted, though an own import of another enum sharing a constructor then wins it

arms.name: M-HOIST-VALUES-BLIND
arms.note: an enum import is hoisted into the ambient source, where its constructors outrank a module's own field imports in either order

arms.name: M-GUARD-REBIND-BLIND
arms.note: a stranded `using` is moved below a guarded import binding the same name, so the LAST statement — and the meaning — changes

arms.name: M-UNUSED-USING-NO-DOOR
arms.note: unused-import stops asking the door

arms.name: M-HOIST-USINGS-SOURCE-ORDER
arms.note: hoisted usings are inserted first-first at a seat that puts each above the first, so they land reversed — and a using order IS its static-extension priority

arms.name: M-HOIST-RECEIVER-UNVOUCHED
arms.note: every governed module is taken to resolve a statement it would receive, so a library import lands in an ambient source governing a module another build compiles without that library, and that build stops on the ambient source

arms.name: M-HOIST-RECEIVER-EVIDENCE-BLIND
arms.note: a receiver's own statements never vouch for the classpath entry it already compiles with, so every statement from a library is withheld wherever one governed module does not spell it

arms.name: M-HOIST-IMPLICIT-TIER-BLIND
arms.note: the language's implicit tier no longer vouches for a receiver, so an allow-listed using of a top-level std module is withheld from every directory where one module spells no other std statement

arms.name: M-HOIST-TIE-NEAREST-FIRST
arms.note: of two sites governing the same modules the nested one is weighed first, so a parent whose every module sits under one child takes the statement its child already took and one chain carries it twice

arms.name: M-SINK-NEVER-SOUND
arms.note: no ambient statement is ever judged safe to send back to its readers, so the reverse direction proposes nothing and a statement one module reads stays in the source of a whole directory

arms.name: M-SINK-SHARE-BLIND
arms.find: if (candidate == null || reading.length == 0 || reading.length * PERCENT >= sink * governed.length) continue;
arms.note: the reader share is never read, so every ambient statement any module reads is sent back into its readers however many of them there are

arms.name: M-SINK-HYSTERESIS-OFF
arms.note: a sink threshold at or above the hoist one is honoured, so one share sits on both sides and a fix run moves the same statement into the ambient source and back out of it pass after pass

arms.name: M-SINK-RIVAL-BLIND
arms.find: if (imp.guarded || SymbolIndex.bindsAnyOf(imp, statement.names, ctx.publicTypes)) return false;
arms.note: a nearer ambient source binding the same name to another type is no rival, so the own copy a sink writes outranks it and the reader's name turns to the sunk statement's type

arms.name: M-SINK-OWN-RIVAL-BLIND
arms.note: a reader's own import of the same name is no rival, so the own copy a sink writes lands beside it and whichever sorts last takes the name

arms.name: M-SINK-USING-RANK-BLIND
arms.find: if (statement.isUsing && imp.kind == ImportKind.Using && ctx.contested(file, statement.path, imp.raw)) return false;
arms.note: another using in the reader's chain is no rival, so a sunk using turns own and outranks it, and every extension method both declare resolves to the sunk one

arms.name: M-EMPTY-AMBIENT-NEVER
arms.note: no ambient source is ever empty, so the file an emptying fix leaves behind stays on disk unreported

arms.name: M-EMPTY-AMBIENT-KEEPS
arms.note: a blank ambient source is reported and never deleted, so every emptying fix leaves its file behind

arms.name: M-SINK-WHOLE-FILE
arms.replace: edits: [{ span: new Span(0, (sourceOf[file] ?? '').length), text: textOf[file] ?? '' }]
arms.note: a sink rewrites each reader as one whole-file edit, so a cross-file rename another rule makes in that reader in the same pass overlaps it and one of the two is lost

arms.name: M-UNUSED-USING-SELF-MENTION
arms.note: the declaring module's own declaration reads as a use of an ambient `using` of it, so a dead one is never reported

arms.name: M-HOIST-BUILDS-UNASKED
arms.note: the run's declared builds are never asked which files each parses, so a receiver no statement of its own vouches for withholds a statement every build reading it already reads

arms.name: M-HOIST-BUILD-WITHOUT-MODULE-IGNORED
arms.note: a build that parses a receiver but not the statement's module no longer withholds the statement, so the ambient source stops that build on an import it cannot resolve

arms.name: M-HOIST-UNPARSED-RECEIVER-WITHHELD
arms.note: a receiver no declared build parses is read as parsed by a build that lacks the statement's module, so a statement is withheld from a directory holding code no build compiles

arms.name: M-HOIST-UNKNOWN-BUILDS-GUESSED
arms.note: a project that declared its build list complete and whose builds the run does not know falls back on classpath evidence, so `--fix --no-oracle` writes an ambient statement into a directory a build of that list compiles without the statement's module

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-SITE-BLIND
arms.note: a value site is shortened whatever binds the short name there, so a local, a module enum constructor or an imported-beside local silently becomes what the expression reads

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-SITE-NEVER
arms.note: no value site is ever shortened, so a static call or a type argument whose short name binds nothing else stays qualified

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-DOORS-SKIPPED
arms.find: && ValueDoors.bindsNoValue(site, name, o.span, info, context.tree, context.shape, file, index);
arms.note: only the file's own text is asked, so a field the enclosing type INHERITS outranks the shortened type at a value site unseen

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-GUARDED-NEVER
arms.note: a `#if` occurrence is never rewritten, so it stays qualified beside an unguarded short use of the name and beside the import its path buys

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-GUARDED-RIDES-FRESH-IMPORT
arms.note: a `#if` occurrence of a path that buys its import keeps the full path, so the guarded spelling ignores the unconditional import the same call adds

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-POSITIONS-ALWAYS
arms.note: value positions are rewritten and counted toward an import although the project never opted them in

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-IMPORT-MIN-USES-IGNORED
arms.note: the project's importMinUses is ignored, so an import is bought at the default count whatever the project declared

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-COUNT-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: occurrences are grouped by how they are spelled, so a hybrid and the module-qualified path of the same type each fall short of the import threshold

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-GUARDED-WITHOUT-SHORT-USE
arms.note: every `#if` occurrence takes the short spelling, even where nothing unguarded in the file writes that name

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-POSITIONS-DEFAULT-OFF
arms.note: value positions are skipped unless the project opts them in, so a static call whose short name the compiler confirms stays qualified

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-UNANSWERED-SKIPPED
arms.note: a value-site rewrite needs no compiler answer, so a build macro's static can silently take over the shortened call

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-REFUSAL-NOT-REPLANNED
arms.note: a refused value site is dropped without planning again, so the import it helped buy stays behind for a single rewrite

arms.name: M-SHORTEN-VALUE-OFFSET-UNSHIFTED
arms.note: the compiler is asked at the original offset in the rewritten text, past the import the same rewrite adds, so it answers about another name
